text: Support for RTCP is REQUIRED, per [RFC3550], and it provides, among other things, the following important functionality in relation to SIPREC:
notes: rtcp => mux | port: the receiver reads the source's RTCP and sends receiver reports, plain or SRTCP; rtcp => none (the default) keeps the receiver without RTCP

text: When sending RTCP, the use of symmetric RTCP is REQUIRED.
notes: reports leave from the socket RTCP is taken on (the RTP port with mux, the port above with port), to where the source's RTCP came from

text: It is important that the SRC and recording-aware UAs generate CNAMEs appropriately and that the SRC and SRS interpret and use them for this purpose.
notes: the source's SDES CNAME is kept per SSRC (stats/1 sources); the receiver's own CNAME is random (RFC 7022) or the cname option

text: This field can be used to distinguish RTP and RTCP packets when two restrictions are observed: 1) the RTP payload type values used are distinct from the RTCP packet types used; and 2) for each RTP payload type (PT), PT+128 is distinct from the RTCP packet types used.
notes: a packet whose second octet is 192 to 223 is RTCP (SR to APP sit where payload types 72 to 76 with the marker would); anything else is RTP

text: The receiver MUST be prepared to receive RTCP packets on the RTP port, and any resource reservation needs to be made including the RTCP bandwidth.
notes: rtcp => mux takes RTCP and SRTCP on the RTP port

text: SR or RR: The first RTCP packet in the compound packet MUST always be a report packet to facilitate header validation as described in Appendix A.2.
notes: every compound packet the receiver sends starts with an RR; parse/1 refuses one that does not start with SR or RR

text: SDES: An SDES packet containing a CNAME item MUST be included in each compound RTCP packet, except as noted in Section 9.1.
notes: each report carries SDES with the receiver's CNAME after the RR

text: Reception statistics (in SR or RR) should be sent as often as bandwidth constraints will allow to maximize the resolution of the statistics, therefore each periodically transmitted compound RTCP packet MUST include a report packet.
notes: each periodic report is an RR with a block per source heard since the last one

text: An implementation SHOULD ignore incoming RTCP packets with types unknown to it.
notes: an unknown packet type is kept by number and ignored, never an atom

text: The RECOMMENDED value for a fixed minimum interval is 5 seconds.
notes: the interval is max(5 s, n * C) times 0.5 to 1.5 (A.7, no reconsideration so no e - 3/2 division)

text: At application startup, a delay SHOULD be imposed before the first compound RTCP packet is sent to allow time for RTCP packets to be received from other participants so the report interval will converge to the correct value more quickly.
notes: the first report waits half the minimum, 2.5 s, times 0.5 to 1.5

text: An implementation which is constrained to two-party unicast operation SHOULD still use randomization of the RTCP transmission interval to avoid unintended synchronization of multiple instances operating in the same environment, but MAY omit the "timer reconsideration" and "reverse reconsideration" algorithms in Sections 6.3.3, 6.3.6 and 6.3.7.
notes: each interval is drawn at random; reconsideration is omitted

text: If the group size estimate members is less than 50 when the participant decides to leave, the participant MAY send a BYE packet immediately.
notes: stopping a receiver that sent a report sends RR, SDES and BYE at once

text: In either case, a participant which never sent an RTP or RTCP packet MUST NOT send a BYE packet when they leave the group.
notes: a receiver stopped before its first report sends nothing

text: fraction lost: The fraction of RTP data packets from source SSRC_n lost since the previous SR or RR packet was sent, expressed as a fixed point number with the binary point at the left edge of the field. If the loss is negative due to duplicates, the fraction lost is set to zero.
notes: lost since the last report times 256 over expected since then (A.3); 0 when duplicates make it negative

text: cumulative number of packets lost: The total number of RTP data packets from source SSRC_n that have been lost since the beginning of reception. extended highest sequence number received: The low 16 bits contain the highest sequence number received in an RTP data packet from source SSRC_n, and the most significant 16 bits extend that sequence number with the corresponding count of sequence number cycles.
notes: expected minus received, which may go negative, clamped to 24 bits; the cycles of A.1 in the top 16 bits

text: The jitter calculation MUST conform to the formula specified here in order to allow profile-independent monitors to make valid interpretations of reports coming from different implementations.
notes: A.8's integer estimator, J += |D| - (J + 8) / 16 scaled by 16, the transit difference taken modulo 2^32

text: The interarrival jitter SHOULD be calculated continuously as each data packet i is received from source SSRC_n, using this difference D for that packet and the previous packet i-1 in order of arrival (not necessarily in sequence).
notes: each RTP packet updates its source's jitter on arrival, at the 8000 Hz G.711 clock

text: last SR timestamp (LSR): The middle 32 bits out of 64 in the NTP timestamp received as part of the most recent RTCP sender report (SR) packet from source SSRC_n. If no SR has been received yet, the field is set to zero. delay since last SR (DLSR): The delay, expressed in units of 1/65536 seconds, between receiving the last SR packet from source SSRC_n and sending this reception report block.
notes: the source's last SR gives LSR; DLSR is the time since it came, in 1/65536 s; both 0 before an SR (checked on the values of figure 2)

text: An empty RR packet (RC = 0) MUST be put at the head of a compound RTCP packet when there is no data transmission or reception to report.
notes: a report with no source heard since the last one is an RR with no block

text: For UDP and similar protocols, RTP SHOULD use an even destination port number and the corresponding RTCP stream SHOULD use the next higher (odd) destination port number.
notes: rtcp => port binds an even port and the next one; reports go to the source's RTP port + 1 until its RTCP is heard

text: Message authentication for RTCP is REQUIRED, as it is the control protocol (e.g., it has a BYE packet) for RTP.
notes: on an SRTP stream the receiver's reports are SRTCP, encrypted and tagged with its own key (srtcp_out); without that key it sends none

text: The SRTCP index MUST be set to zero before the first SRTCP packet is sent, and MUST be incremented by one, modulo 2^31, after each SRTCP packet is sent.
notes: protect_rtcp/2 starts at index 0 and adds one per packet; the key's lifetime past, it sends none

text: In particular, after a re-key, the SRTCP index MUST NOT be reset to zero again.
notes: rekey/2 of chappe_audio_srtp, and rekey/3 of the receiver, keep the index

text: 5. The resulting value of T is divided by e-3/2=1.21828 to compensate for the fact that the timer reconsideration algorithm converges to a value of the RTCP bandwidth below the intended average.
notes: not divided: chappe does no timer reconsideration (6.3 lets a two-party unicast participant omit it), so the compensation would only shorten the average below the 5 s minimum; the interval is max(5 s, n * C) times 0.5 to 1.5

text: Furthermore, to make the transmission rate of RTCP packets more adaptive to changes in group membership, the following "reverse reconsideration" algorithm SHOULD be executed when a BYE packet is received that reduces members to a value less than pmembers:
notes: not run: the session is the receiver and its sender, so a BYE does not move the interval enough to matter; the next interval is drawn from the members left

text: At occasional intervals, the participant MUST check to see if any of the other participants time out.
notes: sources are not timed out: a report carries a block only for a source heard since the last report, a BYE drops its source, the table holds at most 31 sources, and the receiver ends with its recording session

text: Instead, the entry SHOULD be marked as having received a BYE and then deleted after an appropriate delay.
notes: a source's entry is deleted as soon as its BYE comes; a straggler RTP packet starts a new entry, and its statistics start again

text: If a source discovers at any time that another source is using the same SSRC identifier as its own, it MUST send an RTCP BYE packet for the old identifier and choose another random one.
notes: on a collision the receiver draws a new random SSRC for its next report but sends no BYE for the old one: it sends no RTP, and its next report, under the new SSRC, tells the source

text: All participants MUST use the same value for the session bandwidth so that the same RTCP interval will be calculated.
notes: the session bandwidth is fixed at 80 kbit/s (PCMU at 20 ms with headers), RTCP 5% of it; the SDP b= lines are not read. With two members the 5 s minimum decides the interval either way

text: The SR is issued if a site has sent any data packets during the interval since issuing the last report or the previous one, otherwise the RR is issued.
notes: the recording server never sends media, so it always sends RR; it never sends SR, and the sender-side rules (SR sender info, RTP timestamps, sender BYE) do not apply
